questions.question: When adding time crosses midnight (e.g., 11:40 PM + 30 minutes), what happens?
options: It rolls over to the next day, with the hour resetting using modulo 24
The result is simply capped at 11:59 PM
questions.rationale: Crossing midnight means the hour value wraps around (modulo 24) and the date advances by one day — 11:40 PM + 30 minutes becomes 12:10 AM the next day.

questions.question: When subtracting time and the minutes being subtracted are larger than the available minutes, what technique is used?
options: Borrowing: take 60 minutes from the hour value before subtracting
questions.rationale: Just like borrowing in ordinary subtraction, you borrow 60 minutes from the hour column (reducing the hour by 1) before completing the minute subtraction.

questions.question: What does 'elapsed time' measure?
options: The duration between a start time and an end time
questions.rationale: Elapsed time is the duration — the amount of time that has passed — between a given start time and end time.

questions.question: How do you calculate elapsed time when the end time is on the next day (crosses midnight)?
options: Add 24 hours (or the wrap-around amount) to the end time before subtracting the start time
Just subtract the hour digits and ignore minutes
Use only the minutes, ignoring the hour
questions.rationale: When the end time is on the next day, adding 24 hours to it before subtracting the start time correctly accounts for the day boundary crossed.

questions.question: What does 'modular time' mean?
options: Time measured only in modules of software
Time values wrap around using a fixed modulus (12, 24, or 60) rather than increasing without bound
Time that changes with the seasons
questions.rationale: Modular time means the values wrap around at a fixed point (60 for minutes/seconds, 12 or 24 for hours) instead of growing indefinitely.

questions.question: What is 'circular distance' between two times on a clock face?
options: The straight-line ruler distance between the two hand tips
The shorter of the two possible arc distances between them going around the circle
Always exactly half the clock face
The sum of both hands' individual angles from 12
questions.rationale: Circular distance takes the shorter of the two arcs connecting two points around the circular clock face, since you can measure the gap going either direction.

questions.question: In one full revolution, how many degrees does the minute hand travel?
questions.rationale: One full revolution of any clock hand covers the full circle, which is 360 degrees.

questions.question: How many degrees per minute does the minute hand move?
questions.rationale: The minute hand completes 360 degrees in 60 minutes, so it moves 360/60 = 6 degrees per minute.

questions.question: How many degrees per minute does the hour hand move?
questions.rationale: The hour hand completes 360 degrees in 12 hours (720 minutes), so it moves 360/720 = 0.5 degrees per minute.

questions.question: What is the standard clock-angle formula for the angle between the hour and minute hands at H hours and M minutes?
questions.rationale: The standard formula is |30H - 5.5M| degrees, combining the hour hand's 30 degrees-per-hour rate with its extra 0.5 degrees-per-minute drift, against the minute hand's 6 degrees-per-minute rate.
